rubric_items.reason: All five acceptance criteria are covered by REQ-1 to REQ-10. The walk-in motivation, sorting by count and changes to the tile are listed as out of scope, each with a reason.
Most REQs cover one behaviour and can be tested. REQ-10 joins filters and search in one REQ. REQ-4 adds a sum-equality check that holds only under unstated conditions.
Statuses are cited, and REQ-11 is assumed with a real basis. REQ-4 is marked known, but its sum-equals-tile condition is an inference the ticket does not state.
No ticket-baseline clash found. The ticket and baseline agree on the time zone. A possible tile-rule mismatch is raised as Q-05, citing the ticket.
Nothing blocks needlessly and roles fit. Q-02 asks something the ticket already answers (PRD DOC-2). Q-05's default can contradict REQ-3. Some defaults do not match their listed options.
Plain and readable, and glossary terms are used consistently. Minor redundancy between the unknowns and the questions.

findings.text: REQ-4 is marked known but adds a condition the ticket does not state: the sum of all doctors' Today counts equals the tile. This holds only if every doctor is summed, including Inactive and filtered-out ones, across all pages.

cites.quote: so the sum of all doctors' Today counts equals that tile's value for the same moment
counted the same way as the dashboard's "Appointments today" tile

findings.suggested_fix: Limit REQ-4 to 'uses the same counting rule as the tile'. Or move the sum-equality check to assumed, with scope stated as all doctors including Inactive, ignoring filters and paging.

findings.text: Q-05's default reuses the tile's rule even if the tile differs. That would contradict known REQ-3 (exclude only Cancelled), which the ticket states explicitly.

cites.quote: Reuse the tile's counting rule; impact analysis confirms it excludes only Cancelled
The count includes appointments in any status except `Cancelled`.

findings.suggested_fix: Set the default to one of the listed options, e.g. 'Tile differs; follow the ticket and raise a separate fix', so REQ-3 always holds.

findings.text: Q-02 asks whether the doctors list is the PRD DOC-2 page, but the ticket already names DOC-2. This is a needless question.

cites.quote: Is the 'doctors list' the existing doctors list page described by PRD DOC-2?

findings.suggested_fix: Drop Q-02, or turn U-2 into a glossary note that cites ticket L16.

findings.text: The defaults of Q-03 and Q-05 are not among their listed options, so it is unclear which option a default answer selects.

cites.quote: Use existing filters; add any missing doctor/day filter in this change

findings.suggested_fix: Make each default exactly one of its options.

findings.text: REQ-10 joins two behaviours, filters unchanged and search unchanged, in one REQ.

cites.quote: keeps its current `filters and search` with unchanged behaviour

findings.suggested_fix: Split into one REQ for filters and one for search.

findings.text: Claim C8 (Inactive, never deleted) supports no requirement and cites a baseline section the package does not list.

cites.quote: Doctors with appointments are made `Inactive`, never deleted.

findings.suggested_fix: Remove C8, or tie it to a requirement, e.g. whether Inactive doctors show a Today count.

cites.quote: Hospital time zone Asia/Kolkata, currency INR.
The dashboard shows the day in one screen.
tiles that count patients, doctors and appointments, each linking to the list it
selecting it opens the list behind the count
An appointment called off before it took place, with a reason; its slot becomes free again.
The doctors list shows code, name, specialization, department, fee and status
Doctors and patients with appointments are made Inactive, never deleted.

questions.text: Should Inactive doctors with appointments today appear with a Today count? And should REQ-4's sum-equals-tile check span all doctors regardless of list filters and paging?
